items.title: Pug Horton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998
items.q: I’ve worked with performers and I roomed with Maxine Sullivan

ctx.x: I suppose you know I’ve only been blonde for a few years since I started to go gray. I used to be very, very dark. In fact when Gus Johnson met me for the first time he believed that I was black. And I have very dark skin. And I don’t know whether, I don’t think people feel any different regardless of what color they are. I think that there has

been times when I’ve read articles about people not liking a singer because they were of a different colored persuasion you know? But it’s never actually happened to me. I don’t believe so. I’ve worked with performers and I roomed with Maxine Sullivan and I never felt it, and I don’t think anyone ever made me feel conscious of it. The fact that John Hammond — Hank O’Neil once said “you’re the only singer that John Hammond ever said anything nice about except for the ones that he really loved, Billie and Bessie.”…

Well there seems to be some controversy going on in the last few years about the white musicians’ place in jazz today, and whether or not they have usurped the music. And I find it curious that there seems to be very few young black musicians playing what we have come to call classic jazz. At the jazz parties you don’t see many.
